_what: Meaning of the bracketed labels that open some Radheef senses, e.g. '(ސ.) ހަރުގަނޑު.' Established 2026-09-26 from evidence, not from an Academy legend (none was found in the APK or web app).
_evidence: The current Radheef app models each meaning with dialect, specific_usage_atolls (a list), regions, diction_level and literary_class fields; the old DB compresses these into a leading bracket.
Every single-letter label is a real Maldivian atoll code letter (ހ ނ ރ ބ ޅ އ މ ފ ދ ތ ލ ގ ޏ ސ); combinations (ޏ.ސ., ލ.ގ., ގ.ސ.) are multi-atoll usage, matching the list-valued specific_usage_atolls.
The most frequent labels are ސ (Addu), ގ (Huvadhu) and ޏ (Fuvahmulah) -- the three most divergent Dhivehi dialects; (މަލިކު) spells Maliku/Minicoy out in full.

Sound-pattern check against the open comparative-dhivehi-dialect-project data: where standard Dhivehi ends in -u, Huvadhu ends in -e/-aa (15/18); Radheef (ގ.) headwords paired with a standard -u word end in -e/-aa 9/15. Addu (-a/-u) and Fuvahmulah (-o) are consistent at smaller n.

(ބދ.): the web app names a special category 'ބޯދާ ލަފުޒު' (ބ+ދ). Radheef prose uses 'ބޯދާ ޒަމާނު' (Buddhist era) and 'މީގެ ބޯދާ ލަފުޒަކީ …'. The (ބދ.) headwords are Sanskrit/Pali-derived: ބަވަނަ ސުންދުރަ (bhuvana sundara), ހޮބަލޯކަ (loka), ކައްތިރި (kshatriya), މުރަނު (marana).

confidence.ހ = Haa Alif and/or Haa Dhaalu: medium (letter is ambiguous between the two Haa atolls)
